record.paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: Determine the best possible lower bound on the worst-case spanning ratio of the Euclidean Delaunay triangulation. In particular, can one construct a planar point set whose Delaunay triangulation has spanning ratio strictly greater than 1.5932, and can one do so with the points restricted to convex position so that the spanning ratio is strictly greater than 1.581?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 3. What is the best lower bound on the worst-case spanning ratio of the Delaunay triangulation? Can one construct a point set such that the spanning ratio of its Delaunay triangulation is strictly greater than 1.5932? For points in convex position, can one construct a point set such that the spanning ratio is strictly greater than 1.581?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a finite set P of points in the Euclidean plane in general position, let DT(P) denote the Delaunay triangulation of P, i.e., the planar straight-line graph in which a triangle uvw with vertices in P is a face if and only if the open disk with u, v, w on its boundary contains no point of P in its interior. For two points u, v in P, let d_DT(u, v) denote the length (sum of Euclidean edge lengths) of a shortest path between u and v in DT(P), and let |uv| denote the Euclidean distance between u and v. The spanning ratio of DT(P) is defined as
  sr(P) = max_{u,v ∈ P, u ≠ v} d_DT(u, v) / |uv|,
and the worst-case spanning ratio of the Euclidean Delaunay triangulation is
  ρ = sup_{P} sr(P),
where the supremum is taken over all finite point sets P in general position in the plane.

(a) Determine the best possible lower bound on ρ. In particular, exhibit (or prove the nonexistence of) a finite planar point set P such that sr(P) > 1.5932.

(b) Let ρ_conv = sup{ sr(P) : P is a finite point set in convex position in the plane }. Determine the best possible lower bound on ρ_conv. In particular, exhibit (or prove the nonexistence of) a finite point set P in convex position such that sr(P) > 1.581.
artifact.status_search_result: The exact worst-case spanning ratio of the Euclidean Delaunay triangulation remains open. The best known lower bound for general point sets is approximately 1.5932 (Xia and Zhang), with the best known upper bound under 1.998 (Xia). For convex position, lower bounds near 1.58 are known but the gap with the upper bound (~2.33 by Cui–Kanj–Xia) persists. Recent works (2023–2025) have resolved related variants (rectangle, parallelogram, arbitrary-triangle Delaunay graphs) but not the original Euclidean (circle) case.

status_evidence.title: The Tight Spanning Ratio of the Rectangle Delaunay Triangulation
status_evidence.snippet: Studies tight spanning ratios of variant Delaunay triangulations; the Euclidean (circle) case bounds remain 1.5932 lower and <1.998 upper.
status_evidence.claim: The Euclidean Delaunay triangulation spanning ratio is known only to lie between 1.5932 and 1.998.

status_evidence.title: The Stretch Factor of the Delaunay Triangulation Is Less Than 1.998
status_evidence.snippet: Xia proves the upper bound 1.998 on the stretch factor of the Delaunay triangulation.
status_evidence.claim: Best known upper bound is 1.998; lower bound 1.5932 remains best, gap unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Tight Routing and Spanning Ratios of Arbitrary Triangle Delaunay Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Recent paper addressing related triangle Delaunay graphs, indicating the Euclidean case is still open.
status_evidence.claim: Determining the exact spanning ratio of the Euclidean Delaunay triangulation remains an open problem.
